Donetsk "Mushketivske" Municipal Cemetery – Jewish Section

Jewish Cemetery · Donetsk, Ukraine

Not demolished. Donetsk (known as Yuzivka until 1924, then Stalino until 1961) had a Jewish population of 3,168 in 1897, rising sharply to 11,732 (24% of residents) by 1910, despite a three-day pogrom in 1905. By the 1910s the city supported three synagogues, five private Jewish schools, and a Talmud Torah. Under Soviet industrialization, the Jewish population grew in absolute numbers (24,991 by 1939) even as its relative share fell to just 5%. Most Jews evacuated after Germany's 1941 invasion, but roughly 3,000 remained; they were confined to a quarry ghetto in spring 1942 and murdered. The community rebuilt after the war, reaching 22,300 by 1959; despite mass emigration in the 1990s, Jewish institutional life continued, with 5,087 Jews recorded in the 2001 census. This cemetery section was founded in 1929, with the earliest burials dated 1930; older tombstones from other, now-closed cemeteries were relocated here over time.
